name: Telescopium
introduction: is the Telescope, introduced by Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in the 1750s. It is a faint constellation south of Sagittarius.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Observing from the Cape of Good Hope, Lacaille filled the gaps of the southern sky with the instruments of science and art: a microscope, a pendulum clock, an air pump and, here, the telescope that had transformed astronomy a century and a half earlier.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Alpha Telescopii](hip:90422) is a blue-white subgiant about 280 light-years away. [Zeta Telescopii](hip:90568) is an orange giant.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Telescopium contains the globular cluster NGC 6584 and the Telescopium Group, a nearby gathering of galaxies dominated by the elliptical NGC 6868.
